races.name: Grace And Dotty Handicap

runners_data.name: Anglesey Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent runner seeking first win after 20 attempts but recent return should have sharpened him for this assignment
runners_data.comment: Exposed 20-race maiden but often placed and a recent run should have sharpened him up
runners_data.spotlight: Still seeking his first win after 20 attempts but there have been several good runs along the way; recent return from a ten-month layoff should have sharpened him up and he holds each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won last time at Southwell and handles this trip well with late finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Conditions no problem and arrives on the back of an AW win; each-way claims once more
runners_data.spotlight: Produced late when winning a 5f handicap at Southwell three weeks ago; has the ability to defy a 3lb rise and she has run well over C&D in the past; one for the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from Tim Easterby stable with solid recent form over similar trips

runners_data.name: Masterclass
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from break who won comfortably over 5f at Nottingham off higher mark
runners_data.comment: On handy mark and latest Pontefract fourth can be upgraded (wide on home turn); e-w shout
runners_data.spotlight: Ended a losing run when the comfortable winner of a 5f handicap at Nottingham last May (5f, good to firm) off a 1lb higher mark; he was returning from a short break when fourth of 13 at Pontefract 17 days ago and that effort can be upgraded as he was wider than ideal as the field turned for home; each-way shout.

runners_data.name: Newyorkstateofmind
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up runner returning after 169 days with better record on AW than turf
runners_data.comment: Conditions fine and on a dangerous mark so he can't be discounted despite his absence
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran with a better record on AW than turf; 5f on fast ground no problem for him and he has run well after an absence in the past (although not last year); good run wouldn't be a surprise but others appeal more for win purposes.

runners_data.name: Beerwah
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who broke maiden at Beverley last September and ran well next time over course and distance
runners_data.comment: Ended 2025 in good order; still feasibly weighted & he's one to consider back from a break
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the 14th attempt when landing a 5f handicap at Beverley last September (soft) and ran well for fourth of 14 at Musselburgh one month later (good Topspeed figure); could progress further this year and he has shown promise on good to firm.

runners_data.name: Auntie Jo
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won last time in first-time visor and comes here just four days later
runners_data.comment: Three solid runs on AW since fitted with a visor; more to prove on turf but not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Ready win in a first-time visor at Newcastle last month (5f); perfectly good efforts in defeat twice since, coming from well back having blown the start at Newcastle on Monday (6f); more to prove on turf but this should be run to suit.

runners_data.name: Vault Of Heaven
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 157-day break off 2lb lower mark but poor recent Newcastle effort
runners_data.comment: 12-race maiden but capable and he's tumbled down weights; dangerous if the new hood works
runners_data.spotlight: 0-12 and well beaten at Newcastle when last seen in November; he was sent off favourite on that occasion and returns from a break off a 2lb lower mark; no doubt the ability is there to win races if the addition of a hood has a calming effect (often races too freely).

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won at Catterick but ran poorly last time at Thirsk over 6f
runners_data.comment: 5f Catterick win 16 days ago but ran poorly at Thirsk on Saturday (6f); others stronger
runners_data.spotlight: Ran poorly at Thirsk on Saturday (6f) but he had earlier won a 5f handicap at Catterick in determined fashion; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: No Gain
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from new trainer Adam Kirby who showed form returning from long absence last time
runners_data.comment: Promising 4th on stable debut last month (6f, AW); a bigger effort could be brewing
runners_data.spotlight: Tried over as far as 1m4f when trained by Martin Dunne; won a 7f event in Jersey last June; absent for 276 days prior to a close fourth at Wolverhampton last month (6f; first time in these retained accessories), an effort that can be marked up as she made a big move in the middle section of the race while racing on the outside of the field; dropping to 5f is new but a strongly run race at the trip could suit; suspicion a bigger effort is brewing.

runners_data.name: Thank The Lord
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who ended 2025 with placed efforts and races off 6lb lower mark
runners_data.comment: Ended 2025 with two good runs but well short of that level so far in 2026; risky
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with two placed efforts on AW and he lines up here off a 6lb lower mark than when second at Newcastle in December; that is a result of four lesser efforts though and he now has a point to prove.

runners_data.name: Doralee
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was close third to Golden Prosperity at Catterick 16 days ago
runners_data.comment: Just one win from 17 starts but she arrives on the back of a good third at Catterick
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 5f classified event at Redcar last summer; close third to Golden Prosperity at Catterick 16 days ago (5f, good), always prominent; needs a bit more if she's to come out on top in this competitive sprint.

runners_data.name: Isla Bella
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on losing run but Joey Ramsden yard capable and unraced on turf this year
runners_data.comment: Strongly run 5f suits her best; went close on AW last month; each-way shout
runners_data.spotlight: Losing run stands at 17 but she has run some good races in defeat for Joey Ramsden and a strongly run race at this trip should see her to best effect; unraced on faster than good; each-way shout if the ground is no issue.

runners_data.name: Trust Sergei
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won twice last spring including over course and distance on good to firm
runners_data.comment: 6f win here last May off 2lb higher; promise two starts ago but couldn't back it up latest
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive last spring, following a 5f AW win with a ready 6f win at this track (good to firm); mixed bag since then but his penultimate fourth at Wolverhampton was encouraging; failed to back it up ten days later but no doubt the ability is there and he's well handicapped now.

runners_data.name: Lil Wade
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with warning for fading in finish and poor recent form makes easy to swerve
runners_data.comment: Not much to shout about in the last 18 months and easy enough to swerve
runners_data.spotlight: Good runs have been few and far between since his Wolverhampton second in September 2024; easy enough to swerve.

runners_data.name: Ziva's Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on 0-17 record returning from 139-day absence with limited recent promise
runners_data.comment: 17-race maiden with just one handicap run that makes her of interest; absent 139 days
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17 and just one handicap run that makes her of interest, namely her close third at Ripon last July; absent for 139 days and others have more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Tilsworth Ony Ta
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but five-time winner has been well below best on recent evidence
runners_data.comment: Five-time winner but out of sorts so far this year; not a solid option
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time winner but he has been short of his best on AW this year and the return to turf made no difference at Bath 19 days ago; not a solid option.

races.paceDynamic: Thank The Lord is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set a sustainable pace without early pressure from the 17-runner field. Golden Prosperity, Anglesey Lad, Trust Sergei, Doralee and Tilsworth Ony Ta will track in prominent positions behind the leader. The large field will create a strung-out affair with many hold-up horses needing luck in running over the minimum trip. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to the pace and kick, as hold-up horses face significant traffic problems in a big field sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses get first run on Thank The Lord turning for home
scenarios.body: The pace-trackers will have positional advantage and momentum to sweep past the tiring leader in the final furlong. Hold-up horses will struggle to weave through traffic and make up ground over 5f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and gaps open in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: Strong stayers from the back like Opal Storm and Masterclass can utilise their finishing kick when the field spreads out. Their proven ability to win from behind becomes crucial when others stop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Thank The Lord gets soft fractions and kicks clear at the two-pole
scenarios.body: The leader's class tells when given an easy time in front, holding off late challenges. His recent placed efforts suggest he retains ability off this reduced mark.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Thank The Lord stops quickly and prominent horses also tire
scenarios.body: The race becomes a cavalry charge with any horse getting a clear run capable of winning. Form horses with tactical pace like No Gain can capitalise on the carnage.

watchPoints.text: Thank The Lord must be monitored early as the sole pace-setter could dictate the entire race tempo
Traffic problems are inevitable in this 17-runner sprint so watch which hold-up horses get clear runs
Trust Sergei's early position will be crucial as he needs to avoid getting shuffled back in the big field
Opal Storm's finishing kick timing is critical as she must find gaps late in a crowded finish
Golden Prosperity's recovery from poor Thirsk run last weekend needs assessing in the market

races.name: Summer Saturday Series Handicap

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with rare turf appearance but strong all-weather form suggests adaptability to this tactical scenario
runners_data.comment: Ran well latest (AW); rare foray on grass but not dismissed from his lower turf mark
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins (7f/1m, all AW) and it was a good effort when third in Southwell series final (1m, AW) 17 days ago; having a rare foray on grass but did finish second in good-ground Chester handicap (6f) in September; not dismissed from his lower turf mark.

runners_data.name: Mecca's Symphony
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from long absence but showed promise over course and distance last season
runners_data.comment: Promise on this card last year; unexposed and drops in grade for comeback; considered
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race maiden whose reappearance third over C&D (good to firm) contained promise on this card last year; just one run subsequently and she's been off since wind surgery in June; unexposed and drops in grade for this comeback; needs considering, particularly if gaining market traction.

runners_data.name: Singoura
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose best efforts came over course and distance on similar going conditions
runners_data.comment: Likes it here and shaped like she can build on last month's C&D effort after a break
runners_data.spotlight: 1-2 (AW) as a juvenile and although winless last term her best efforts both came over C&D (good to firm); midfield finish (C&D, good to soft) after two-month break wasn't devoid of promise last time; interesting.

runners_data.name: Ey Up He's A Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with recent good form who can travel smoothly from wide draw and time his run
runners_data.comment: Close third (7f, good) on return to turf a fortnight ago; chance off same mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Newcastle (AW) in September and it was a close third at Thirsk (also 7f, good) on his return to turf a fortnight ago; drawn on the wing but can travel smoothly and should be in the thick of it off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Finn Ironside
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with tongue-tie applied, proven ability to make all in big fields
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; step back in the right direction latest; considered
runners_data.spotlight: Made virtually all in big-field York handicap (good to firm) in 2024; C&D (good to soft; first-time tongue-tie) and AW (also 7f) winner last summer; lesser efforts followed until a firm step back in the right direction last time and returns to turf from a handy mark; respected.

runners_data.name: Yafaarr
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good current form with tongue-tie, looked rusty on turf return but better expected
runners_data.comment: Rusty on turf return a fortnight ago; candidate to build on that; first-time tongue-tie
runners_data.spotlight: In decent nick on AW for this yard since August, in the frame all seven starts and scoring at Newcastle (1m) in October; looked rusty on his turf reappearance a fortnight ago but he's a candidate to build on that; first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Pianoforte
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping up to 7f after recent 6f efforts, headgear changes show connections experimenting
runners_data.comment: 0-9 for this yard; career-low mark and second go at this trip the straws to clutch at
runners_data.spotlight: Got up late to win Bath novice (5f, good to firm) for Andrew Balding in June; 0-9 for this yard (majority 6f, turf/AW) and first-time cheekpieces (removed) didn't spark an improved effort last time; career-low mark and second go at this trip (first is easily excused) the straws to clutch at.

runners_data.name: Clasina
runners_data.comment: Market support before a winning stable debut; up 7lb for this reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Attracted market interest on first go for John Berry and it was rewarded with a win at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) in August; up 7lb and absent since so interesting to see how she goes in the market this time.

runners_data.name: The New Bay Pearl
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with new connections after wind surgery, unknown quantity but showed ability for previous yard
runners_data.comment: Has ability but inconsistent; watch the market on reappearance/stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 for Roger Varian but displayed clear ability on AW (tailed off on sole turf start) while also lacking consistency; sold for 5,000gns in December and wind surgery swiftly followed; market might help on this reappearance/stable debut.

runners_data.name: Pearly Squirrel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner and course winner who missed break last time, early position crucial for chances
runners_data.comment: C&D winner who can miss the break; solid on AW of late; could have a say
runners_data.spotlight: C&D (good to firm; first-time cheekpieces) winner in July who also won 7f handicap (AW; no headgear) in March; missed the break (not for the first time) a fortnight ago but otherwise could have a say back on turf.

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with new trainer after previous connections success, adapting to new methods
runners_data.comment: No immediate encouragement on stable debut a fortnight ago
runners_data.spotlight: Came good for Stella Barclay with last-gasp win at Carlisle (7f, good) in August but signed off for that yard with big soft-ground defeat the following month; no immediate encouragement on stable debut a fortnight ago.

runners_data.name: Yehudi
runners_data.note: Prominent type wearing full headgear combination with 7lb claiming jockey, goes close without winning
runners_data.comment: 0-16 (includes turf); had this headgear combination when fourth (AW) latest
runners_data.spotlight: 0-16 (includes turf) but has gone close a couple of times on AW; wore this headgear combination when fourth at Wolverhampton (8.5f, AW) under Hope Regan three weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Reginald Charles
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with rare turf success chance, strong recent all-weather form suggests confidence returning
runners_data.comment: Running well with races spaced out; player if this doesn't come too soon
runners_data.spotlight: 0-16 on turf but he went mighty close at Redcar (good) in October; narrow winner at Southwell (also 7f, AW) on next start in December and it was a good effort when third to Wrydcroft over latter C&D last time; that did come after another two-month break but he's a player if backing it up 17 days on.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for in-form Irish trainer, limited turf experience but yard firing lately

runners_data.name: Onemorenomore
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent course record including winning this race division previously
runners_data.comment: Won division of this in 2024; mark fine; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Good record here with three wins including a division of this (soft; acts on good/good to firm) in 2024; cashed in on reduced mark to open AW account over 7f in November and just 1lb higher on this return to turf after three months away; possibilities.

runners_data.name: Wrydcroft
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in red-hot form with three wins from last four starts, big field specialist
runners_data.comment: Won three of his last four including AW return; has to be of interest under a 3lb nudge
runners_data.spotlight: Won three of his last four, comprising two wins at Leicester (good to soft) and an AW success at Southwell (also 7f) on this month's comeback; big field no bother and he has to be of interest under a 3lb nudge.

runners_data.name: Born A Rebel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tongue-tie who can miss break, needs clean getaway to utilise closing kick
runners_data.comment: Three turf wins; never dangerous on AW return in February but might do better this time
runners_data.spotlight: Can miss the break but scored twice last year, a 20-1 win at Newmarket (good to firm) in July supplemented by a Yarmouth (also 7f, good to soft) success in September; never dangerous on AW return in February but might do better this time.

races.paceDynamic: Finn Ironside is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and should get an uncontested lead with the prominent runners Giant, Mecca's Symphony, Singoura, Pearly Squirrel and Yehudi likely to settle behind him. This sets up a sustainable pace scenario where the leader won't be pressured early, allowing the large pack of hold-up horses including Ey Up He's A Star, Yafaarr, Pianoforte, Wrydcroft and Onemorenomore to get into contention. The tactical verdict strongly favours hold-up horses who can close from off the pace, as Finn Ironside's uncontested lead will create the perfect setup for closers to time their runs in a big field sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Finn Ironside gets an easy lead and the prominent horses settle kindly behind him
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace allows hold-up horses to close strongly in the final two furlongs as the leader and prominent runners come back to them. This scenario perfectly suits the strong contingent of closers who can pick up the pieces late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Apply Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Giant, Singoura or Pearly Squirrel decide to press Finn Ironside from the outset
scenarios.body: A faster early pace stretches the field and creates a more tactical affair where the prominent runners can dominate proceedings. Those settling closer to the pace gain a crucial positional advantage over the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Finn Ironside gets completely uncontested fractions and kicks clear entering the straight
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage as the field fails to organise a challenge early enough in the home straight. His proven ability to make all at York shows he can execute this tactic successfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Suits Versatile Types
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates traffic problems and an uneven gallop with multiple pace angles
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical lottery where positioning and racing luck matter more than pure pace preferences. Horses with tactical speed who can adapt to circumstances hold the edge.

watchPoints.text: Watch Finn Ironside's early fractions as he's the only front-runner and any pressure could compromise his stamina reserves
Monitor Giant's adaptation to turf racing after strong all-weather form, as surface switch adds uncertainty to prominent tactics
Watch for Pearly Squirrel's start after missing the break last time, as early position is crucial for prominent runners
Observe how the Irish raiders Ziggy's Angel and Born A Rebel handle the occasion, as both have tactical speed to be involved
Check market moves on The New Bay Pearl with new trainer and wind surgery, as any support could indicate improvement expected

runners_data.name: Celtic Chariot
runners_data.comment: 45,000gns yearling; sold unraced for 1,000gns last October; likely best watched on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Fetched 55,000gns as a foal and 45,000gns as a yearling but went through the ring for just 1,000gns last October; second foal; half-brother to Canadian 7f AW winner Vrana; dam French Listed-placed 6.5f 2yo winner (RPR 90); likely best watched on debut.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.comment: 240,000gns yearling; dam a useful and well-related winner; can play a part on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 240,000gns yearling; second foal of an 8.6f/1m3f winner (including US; RPR 98), herself a half-sister to winners Gifts Of Gold (smart 1m1f-1m7f) and Dusky Queen (7f Listed); appealing pedigree and no surprise to see him play a part on debut.

runners_data.name: Moreedd
runners_data.comment: Top-class pedigree; represents a powerful stable and is of obvious interest on paper
runners_data.spotlight: Top-class pedigree, closely related to three winners, notably Group 1 winner Benbatl (RPR 124) and a half-brother to three other winners including 1000 Guineas heroine Elmalka (113); dam a Grade/Group 1 winner over 1m2f (118); five of those six winning siblings were successful first time out; of obvious interest.

runners_data.name: Bunyola Bay
runners_data.comment: Well backed when third in a Newbury maiden (6.5f, soft) last October; open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Finished third of eight, beaten 3l, when the well-backed favourite for a 6.5f maiden at Newbury last October (soft; winner has since finished fourth in the Greenham); could see his race out more strongly on the sounder surface; big player.

runners_data.name: Balmoral Boy
runners_data.comment: Minor promise in two AW runs (1m/7f) this spring; handicaps will provide better openings
runners_data.spotlight: Signs of ability in two runs at Newcastle this spring (1m/7f); likely to find life easier once handicapping.

runners_data.name: Deported
runners_data.comment: Useful ability but can over-race and isn't progressing; still a key player in this field
runners_data.spotlight: Free-going sort; has shown a fair level of ability in his four starts and has the strongest form on offer; could do with settling better though and appears vulnerable to anything progressive.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Toastmaster
runners_data.note: Prominent runner perfectly placed to capitalize on the expected pace clash, with consistent handicap form over similar trips
runners_data.comment: Six-race maiden but he's run well in all three handicaps and the drop to 1m may help
runners_data.spotlight: Seeking his first win but he has run well in defeat in all three handicap starts (9.4f-1m3f); drops back to 1m today and he could still have a bit more to offer.

runners_data.name: Welbury
runners_data.note: Steps up from winning 1m novice debut to handicaps, prominent style suits the likely honest pace
runners_data.comment: Strong at the finish in a 1m AW novice last month; more to come in handicaps; yard in form
runners_data.spotlight: Well on top at the finish of a 1m novice at Southwell on his seasonal return five weeks ago; that was his first attempt at the trip and he moves into handicaps with potential and his stable going well.

runners_data.name: Silver State
runners_data.note: Natural leader with recent handicap wins when dominating, but faces genuine pace pressure from Saxophonist
runners_data.comment: 3-5 since handicapping and he bolted up at Bath last week; faster ground today; contender
runners_data.spotlight: He made an instant impact once handicapping in a visor, winning over 8.6f at Wolverhampton in February and following up over 1m at Newcastle 11 days later; back on the up with an emphatic front-running success at Bath last week (1m, good to soft) and he is 2lb well in under a 6lb penalty; faster ground to contend with today but this will be his last chance in a Class 5 for a while and he has to be high on the list.

runners_data.name: Saxophonist
runners_data.note: Fellow front runner returning from 185-day break, market support crucial to assess readiness on handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Promise twice on AW last year; bred to be useful; check betting on handicap/seasonal debut
runners_data.spotlight: Two third-place finishes last season, both over 7f on AW; bred to be useful and market support would look significant on this seasonal and handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Tarmonbarry Kid
runners_data.note: Prominent runner gelded since last seen, could benefit from the operation but needs to prove 1m suits
runners_data.comment: Of interest on his turf debut last summer; 1m should suit now handicapping; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: Promising debut at Chester last July (7f, good; form worked out); no progress in two 7f runs at Newcastle afterwards but he has been gelded prior to his handicap/seasonal debut and stepping up to 1m should suit; one to be interested in.

runners_data.name: Booziebrunch
runners_data.note: Only confirmed hold-up horse in the field, recent Southwell second suggests good current form
runners_data.comment: Good second on his seasonal return this month; perhaps vulnerable to less-exposed sorts
runners_data.spotlight: Stepped up on his 2yo efforts when finishing second to a handicap blot at Southwell three weeks ago (1m); should give his running but perhaps vulnerable to less-exposed sorts.

runners_data.name: Attention Seeker
runners_data.note: Free-going sort who hung badly last time, hard ride likely and may struggle with the pace dynamics
runners_data.comment: Yet to fire for this yard and he looked a hard ride last time; risky on the back of that
runners_data.spotlight: Free-going sort; not matched 2yo form (for Harry Eustace) in three runs for new connections and he looked a hard ride at Wolverhampton last month, hanging badly right throughout; risky on the back of that.

races.paceDynamic: Silver State and Saxophonist are both natural front runners who will clash for the early lead in this 7-runner field. Silver State has shown his best form when allowed to dominate, while Saxophonist returns from a 185-day break but has led in previous starts. Behind them, Toastmaster, Welbury, and Tarmonbarry Kid will sit prominent, with only Booziebrunch likely to be held up. This sets up a genuinely run race with sustained pressure on the leaders throughout, strongly favoring horses that can track the pace and deliver their challenge from prominent positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Silver State and Saxophonist duel early and weaken
scenarios.body: The pace clash allows Toastmaster and Welbury to strike from their tracking positions, benefiting from the honest gallop without doing the donkey work. Their prominent style perfectly suits this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Silver State Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Silver State breaks cleanest and gets first run on Saxophonist
scenarios.body: His recent handicap wins came from leading throughout, and with Rose Dawes' 5lb claim he can dictate terms and kick clear when it matters. The shorter break gives him a fitness edge over his main pace rival.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Saxophonist Returns Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the 185-day break has freshened Saxophonist up significantly
scenarios.body: Daniel Tudhope can use his experience to steal a march on Silver State early, with the fresh horse having enough in reserve for the finish. Market support would confirm this theory.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is suicidal between the two leaders
scenarios.body: Booziebrunch can use his hold-up style to devastating effect, picking off tired horses as the only runner not committed to the early pace battle. His recent Southwell second suggests he's in good form.

watchPoints.text: Silver State and Saxophonist's early battle - if both go too hard they'll set it up for the prominent trackers
Market support for Saxophonist on his return from 185 days off - significant money would suggest he's ready
Attention Seeker's tendency to hang badly when racing keenly could see him compromise his position
Tarmonbarry Kid showing any early speed - the gelding operation may have changed his racing style
Booziebrunch getting a clear run in the straight as the only hold-up horse in a pace-heavy field

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: Leading unchallenged after 218 days off, with Daniel Tudhope able to dictate fractions but may lack race fitness for sustained kick
runners_data.comment: Progressive in 2025 until a low-key run in September; trainer runs two here; market useful
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive as a 3yo, winning at Lingfield (1m2f, good to firm) and Leicester (1m4f, good); below par on her final start in 2025 but she reportedly boiled over in the preliminaries; still has low mileage; market useful with the stable also running Myrrh.

runners_data.name: Nanny Park
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but new stable since October sale and 193 days off create uncertainty about current ability

runners_data.spotlight: Fitted with headgear for the first time at Thirsk two weeks ago (1m, good; turf debut) and ran her best race so far, keeping on for a never-dangerous sixth of 13 (beaten 3.75l); should stay this trip and she is open to further progress.

races.paceDynamic: Percy's Daydream will lead unopposed from the flag with eight hold-up horses tracking behind, creating a sustainable tempo that should see her lasting longer than usual. The lack of pace pressure means the early fractions will be modest, setting up a sprint finish from the 2f pole where the closers can unleash their kicks. With Little Miss India, Ablon, and Myrrh all possessing finishing speed over this staying trip, the patient riders will have every chance to time their challenges. This race shape strongly favors hold-up horses who can quicken off the moderate gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Lasts
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream gets soft fractions and the field comes too late
scenarios.body: The lone pace-setter gets an armchair ride for 10f before finding enough in the tank to repel late challenges. Her sustainable style and 218-day break work in her favor when the kick comes.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses time their runs perfectly in the final 2f
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows multiple closers to wind up together, with the classiest finishers prevailing in a bunch finish. Ablon and Little Miss India's recent form gives them the edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream goes too fast early or the pace quickens unexpectedly
scenarios.body: The race becomes a true test of staying power where the most genuine stayers benefit from the strong gallop. Myrrh's pedigree and Saliko's 1m2f victories become crucial assets.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream goes too slow and creates a messy sprint finish
scenarios.body: The crawling pace leads to a cavalry charge where positioning and luck matter more than class. Any hold-up horse getting a clear run can capitalize on the scramble.

watchPoints.text: Percy's Daydream's early fractions - if she goes too fast the race dynamics completely flip toward the stayers
Little Miss India's break from the stalls - her slow starts could be fatal if she gets too far back in a small field
Ablon's positioning turning for home - her recent front-running win suggests she may need to be closer than usual
The general pace through the first half-mile - if it's crawling it becomes a lottery sprint rather than a staying test
Myrrh's finishing kick after 193 days off - her class is obvious but fitness after the long break remains unproven

races.paceDynamic: Berkshire Schmokin is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the outset without early pressure. With prominent runners Tommo's Ginjaninja, Rumbustious, and Frustration likely to track but not challenge early, the pace will be steady and sustainable through the first half. The large contingent of hold-up horses including Kiss For An Angel, Cotton Bud, Brave Leader, and Madjid will create a backlog that must rely on the final 2-3 furlongs for their challenge. This tactical setup heavily favours prominent racers and the lone front-runner, as they can control fractions and have first run on the patient closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Berkshire Schmokin establishes an uncontested lead and dictates steady fractions.
scenarios.body: P J McDonald can judge the pace perfectly without early pressure, allowing his mount to kick clear when the field comes under pressure. The hold-up brigade will struggle to peg back the controlled advantage over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Victory
scenarios.trigger: If Tommo's Ginjaninja or Rumbustious travel strongly behind the leader and strike at the optimal moment.
scenarios.body: The prominent runners can monitor Berkshire Schmokin's move and time their challenge perfectly, having the tactical advantage of racing handy without doing the early donkey work. Their finishing kick proves decisive as the leader weakens and hold-up horses arrive too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Berkshire Schmokin goes too fast early or the prominent runners press him into stronger fractions.
scenarios.body: The early pace becomes unsustainable, causing the leaders to weaken significantly in the final furlong. This opens the door for the strongest finishing hold-up horses to sweep past, with Kiss For An Angel and Cotton Bud best positioned to capitalize.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Weak Pace Drag
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling slow with no pressure on Berkshire Schmokin through halfway.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 3f pole, heavily favouring horses with tactical pace who can quicken off the bridle. Berkshire Schmokin maintains his advantage through superior positioning, while the best hold-up horses struggle to make up ground in time.

watchPoints.text: Berkshire Schmokin could get an uncontested lead and prove very hard to peg back if allowed to dictate his own fractions
Kiss For An Angel's 171-day absence and gelding operation create uncertainty about his current fitness and attitude
The large number of hold-up horses could create traffic problems turning for home if they're all looking for racing room
Tommo's Ginjaninja's prominent style and recent improvement make him the biggest threat to the front-runner
Watch the early fractions - if Berkshire Schmokin goes too freely early, it opens the door for the closers
